Research areas

Three curricula, one research community

All students share a common core of research methods, then specialise in one of three curricula.

Economics

Theoretical and empirical research on growth, labour markets, public policy, regional development and economic behaviour, with modern econometric and experimental methods.

  • Macroeconomics and growth
  • Labour, health and public economics
  • Regional, tourism and migration economics
  • Behavioural and experimental economics
  • Industrial organisation and digital markets
Meet the Economics facultyCareer prospects

Business and Management

Research on how firms and public organisations innovate, govern themselves, measure performance and create value for customers and society.

  • Innovation and entrepreneurship
  • Corporate governance and accounting
  • Marketing and digital business
  • Public management and performance
  • Tourism and destination management
Meet the Business and Management facultyCareer prospects

Quantitative Methods

Statistical and computational methods for economic and business data, from machine learning and data science to causal inference and financial risk.

  • Statistical and machine learning
  • Computational statistics and data mining
  • Text and social media analytics
  • Causal inference and multivariate analysis
  • Financial risk and stochastic modelling
Meet the Quantitative Methods facultyCareer prospects

Research abroad

Six months at a university abroad

Every PhD student spends at least six months at a university or research centre abroad, working with researchers in their field. So far, students of cycles XXXIII to XL have been hosted by 48 institutions in 16 countries, from LSE and Warwick to Toronto and HEC Montréal.

Careers

Where our graduates go

Of the 100 PhD graduates whose current position we know, 65 work in academia, at universities in Italy and abroad — from Warwick and Manchester to Madrid, Budapest and Santiago de Chile. 29 work outside Italy, in 15 countries, including at the European Central Bank, the European Commission and the OECD.

The Programme

A three-year doctoral programme of the Department of Economics and Business Sciences, training researchers for academic and non-academic careers.

  • Overview
  • Research abroad

Overview

The International PhD Programme in Economics and Business (Dottorato in Scienze Economiche e Aziendali) prepares students to carry out independent, rigorous research and to publish it in international outlets. It brings together economists, business and management scholars and statisticians, so that students learn to combine different perspectives and methods around a research question.

In the first year students attend advanced courses taught in English. From the second year they focus on their thesis, present their work at PhD Days, conferences and summer schools, and usually spend a research period at a university abroad.

Testo da allineare alla parte descrittiva della Scheda di dottorato del XLII ciclo.

  • Positionssee the call for applications

Three curricula, two teaching tracks

Courses are organised in two tracks — one for the Economics and Quantitative Methods curricula, one for the Business and Management curriculum. Each track includes 140 hours of lectures, with shared modules such as Statistics and Research Lab I and II and curriculum-specific modules. In addition, supervisors can arrange personalised courses.

Economics

Growth and macroeconomics, labour, health and public economics, regional and tourism economics, behavioural and experimental economics, industrial organisation.

Faculty (17)

Business and Management

Innovation and entrepreneurship, corporate governance and accounting, marketing and digital business, public management, tourism and destination management.

Faculty (21)

Quantitative Methods

Statistical and machine learning, computational statistics, text and social media analytics, causal inference, financial risk and stochastic modelling.

Faculty (7)

Career prospects

The PhD prepares for research careers in universities and research institutions, and for analytical and managerial roles in public and private organisations. Possible paths for each curriculum:

Economics

  • Universities and research centresPost-doctoral and tenure-track positions in economics; research institutes and think tanks.
  • Central banks and international organisationsEconomic research, forecasting and policy analysis.
  • Public administrationsEconomic planning, design and evaluation of public policies, analysis of macroeconomic aggregates, at national and regional level.
  • Economic consultingStudies and impact assessments for firms, banks and institutions.

Business and Management

  • Universities and business schoolsResearch and teaching in management, accounting, marketing and finance.
  • Firms in every sectorFinancial management and reporting, human resources, internal control and risk management, strategic planning.
  • Consulting and professional firmsManagement consulting, audit and advisory.
  • Public and non-profit organisationsManagement, accounting and performance evaluation; innovation and entrepreneurship support.

Quantitative Methods

  • Universities and research centresResearch and teaching in statistics, data science and quantitative methods.
  • Official statistics and research institutesCollection and analysis of socio-economic data, survey design, evaluation studies.
  • Banks, insurance and financeRisk management, quantitative analysis and model validation.
  • Data science and statistical consultingData analysis, machine learning and decision support for firms and public bodies.

Your three years

The typical path through the programme. The research period abroad usually takes place in the second or third year.

Year 1Advanced training
  • 140 hours of courses in your track, taught in English
  • Mandatory courses in the first semester, electives in the second
  • First outline of the research project
Year 2Research and mobility
  • Supervisor and co-supervisor appointed by the Faculty board after the first year
  • Development of the thesis chapters or papers
  • A research period of at least six months at a university abroad — see where our students have been
  • Conferences, summer schools and workshops
  • Progress presentation at the PhD Days
Year 3Thesis and defence
  • Completion of the thesis
  • Evaluation by two external referees
  • Final defence
  • Optional Doctor Europaeus label or co-tutelle with a foreign university

International by design

  • Courses, seminars and supervision in English
  • Research periods at universities abroad — see where our students have been
  • Doctor Europaeus label and co-tutelle agreements with foreign universities
  • Inaugural lectures by leading scholars from Chicago, Columbia, Wharton and Cornell
  • Member of EDAMBA, the European network of doctoral programmes in management

A supportive research environment

  • A supervisor and a co-supervisor for every student
  • PhD Days and seminars to present work in progress and receive feedback
  • University support for Open Access publishing and research data management
  • Training in research ethics, open science, digital skills and science communication
  • The University of Cagliari holds the HR Excellence in Research award; the programme follows the European Charter for Researchers

Sede, date e fonte di ogni visiting sono nel file «verifica-visiting.csv»; con le note attive i casi da completare sono segnati nell'elenco qui sotto.
  • Ho incluso solo i periodi di studio e ricerca all'estero, non convegni, summer school o brevi visite. La richiesta di Andrea Mottola per IE University (gennaio–marzo 2027) è in attesa del prossimo Collegio e non è in mappa.
  • «Abroad now» si aggiorna da solo a ogni apertura della pagina: un visiting è arancione dal giorno di inizio a quello di fine compresi, dal giorno dopo torna blu. Servono entrambe le date. In WordPress, con un plugin di mappe standard o con Google My Maps, i colori sono fissi: per il cambio automatico serve un piccolo script, da chiedere all'ufficio web; altrimenti si cambiano a mano quando finisce un periodo.
  • Nomi dei dottorandi visibili come nella mappa attuale: decidere se mostrarli o indicare solo ciclo e sede.
  • In WordPress serve un plugin per le mappe (per esempio Leaflet Map), da chiedere all'Ateneo. In alternativa si aggiorna la Google My Maps e si mette il link, come adesso, con l'elenco qui sotto nella pagina.

PhD supervision

Current Alessandro Setzu XLI

  • Interessi di ricerca: quelli di Carroni vengono dal suo sito; quelli di Balia, Brau, Floris e Moro li ho ricavati dai titoli delle loro pubblicazioni, perché le pagine UniCa non hanno una sezione sugli interessi. Vanno fatti confermare ai docenti.
  • Supervisione (34 docenti). I dottorandi in corso vengono dal file delle supervisioni di ottobre 2026; gli ex dottorandi dai relatori indicati nelle tesi in archivio (dati dell'archivio e frontespizi) e, per chi non ha la tesi online, dai documenti del Collegio. Mancano soprattutto i cicli più vecchi, di cui non ci sono fonti. I temi sono le parole chiave delle tesi, più quelli di 7 dottorandi in corso ricavati dai documenti del Collegio: vanno confermati con i dottorandi. I supervisor che non fanno parte del Collegio attuale (per esempio Paci, Mattana, Merella, Del Chiappa) non hanno una scheda.
  • Ogni scheda ha il link alla pagina docente sul sito di Ateneo (45 su 45, verificati il 23/11/2026). Per Castriotta, Nieddu, Floris, Masala e Modica l'indirizzo usa un nome diverso da quello del sito del dottorato (per esempio «emanuele_castriotta»); per Di Guardo, Di Liberto e Licio è la scheda della rubrica. Profili Google Scholar: 40 su 45, trovati con un motore di ricerca e accettati solo se il profilo indica l'Università di Cagliari o un'email unica.it verificata; per gli altri il profilo non c'è o non è stato trovato.
  • In WordPress: blocco "info-cards" del tema oppure colonne; il filtro per area è facoltativo.

  • Posizioni ricontrollate a novembre 2026: 53 coerenti con una fonte trovata online, 13 aggiornate, 8 indicate o confermate dal Gruppo di lavoro, 3 da verificare; per le altre non ho trovato fonti e restano come sul sito attuale.   • Aggiunti 16 dottori di ricerca (cicli XXXV–XXXVIII) che mancavano nella tabella del sito: risultano dai verbali e dai materiali per gli esami finali. Per loro la posizione attuale va ancora raccolta.
  • Tesi: 103 hanno un link, al testo completo (IRIS di UniCa o deposito legale nazionale) oppure, soprattutto per i cicli più vecchi, alla scheda del catalogo delle biblioteche (SBN). Per 4 c'è solo il titolo, preso da un CV, perché la tesi non è online. Ne mancano ancora 10 (per esempio Rashkova, Hettiarachchi, Sulis): si possono aggiungere a mano. Link e titoli sono anche nel file «verifica-posizioni-alumni.csv».
  • Parole chiave delle tesi: 13 vengono dall'archivio IRIS; le altre 56 le ho ricavate io dal titolo e dall'abstract. Sono da far controllare ai supervisor o agli autori. Si possono usare anche nel campo di ricerca, per esempio scrivendo «tourism» o «labour».
  • Numeri calcolati su 117 nomi, 100 con posizione nota. Settore e paese li ho attribuiti io: da verificare. Prima di pubblicare conviene chiedere conferma agli interessati.
  • Mancano i cicli XXII, XXV, XXVII e XXVIII: ci sono dottori di ricerca da aggiungere?

Home / Admissions

Admissions

We welcome applications from graduates in economics, business, statistics and related fields, from Italy and abroad.

Admissions status

  • Cycle XLII (2026/27) — applications closed on 28 September 2026.
  • Cycle XLIII (2027/28) — the call for applications is expected in summer 2027. da confermare
Call for applications, cycle XLII
Pagina da aggiornare a ogni bando. Tutto ciò che è segnato "da verificare" va controllato sul bando del XLIII ciclo prima di pubblicare.
Requisiti, documenti, selezione, borse e date di questa pagina vengono dal bando del XLII ciclo (D.R. n. 856 del 7/8/2026) e dalla scheda del dottorato allegata al bando, nella versione inviata dal Collegio il 22/07/2026. Per posti e borse vale il bando: la scheda di luglio indicava 7 posti e 6 borse. Il bando non pone limiti di età o di residenza per le borse. Nella versione inglese della scheda manca la classe 60/S (Relazioni internazionali), che c'è in quella italiana: da correggere nel prossimo bando.

Who can apply

Candidates of any nationality who, by the application deadline, hold a master's degree in one of the fields accepted by the programme, which include economics, business, finance, statistics, mathematics and computer science: dal bando del XLII ciclo e dalla scheda del dottorato

  • an Italian laurea magistrale in one of the classes listed below, the corresponding laurea specialistica or an equivalent pre-reform degree;
  • a degree obtained abroad that is comparable in duration, level and content and gives access to doctoral programmes in the country where it was awarded. The selection committee assesses its eligibility.

You can also apply before graduating, if you graduate by the date set in the call (31 October 2026 for cycle XLII). You are then admitted with reservation and must obtain the degree before enrolling.

In the call for cycle XLII, one funded position is reserved for international candidates with a degree obtained abroad. They are selected on their CV, reference letters and an online interview.

Why apply

Funded positions

In the call for cycle XLII, four of the five positions came with a three-year scholarship of €16,243 gross a year, increased by 50% during authorised periods abroad. No tuition fees. dal bando del XLII ciclo

Research-led training

A first year of advanced courses in English, then a thesis developed with a supervisor and a co-supervisor.

International experience

Research periods abroad, international speakers and a European network of doctoral programmes.

Strong career outcomes

About six in ten of our graduates work in academia, and three in ten work abroad — at universities, the ECB, the European Commission and the OECD.

How to apply dal bando del XLII ciclo

  1. Read the call for applicationsPublished on the University website with a sheet for each programme, it sets out positions, scholarships, requirements and deadlines.
  2. Explore our researchLook at the curricula and at our faculty's research interests to shape your research proposal.
  3. Prepare your documentsBesides the documents required by the call (transcript of exams and grades, translated into Italian or English for degrees obtained abroad, and an ID or passport), a motivation letter of up to 4,000 characters and a research proposal of up to 6,000 characters with objective, relevant literature, methodology and references. A reference letter is optional, and mandatory for the reserved position: the referee sends it directly to the University, using its form.
  4. Apply onlineOn the PICA platform, by the deadline (28 September 2026 for cycle XLII), paying the €26.80 application fee.
  5. SelectionEvaluation of qualifications and CV, then an interview in person, which can be held online only for justified reasons. Candidates for the reserved position are interviewed online. Interviews take place in October.
  6. Results and enrolmentRankings are published on PICA and on the University website. Admitted candidates enrol by the deadline announced there, and the programme starts in November (16 November 2026 for cycle XLII).

Scholarships

The call for cycle XLII offered 5 positions: 4 with a scholarship and 1 without. Three scholarships were funded by the University of Cagliari and one by the Sardinia Region with European Social Fund Plus resources, for a research project on digital technologies. One of the funded positions was reserved for international candidates with a degree obtained abroad. In every call, the number of scholarships may increase if further funding becomes available. There are no tuition fees: each year PhD students pay only a €16 stamp duty and, if due, the €140 regional tax for the right to university study. dal bando del XLII ciclo

Questions?

Application procedure, enrolment and scholarships: University PhD Office (Dottorati e Master), dottoratiemaster@unica.it.
The programme: see Contacts.

Frequently asked questions

Is the programme taught in English?
Yes. Courses and seminars are in English, and many of our students come from abroad. The admission interview can also be held in English on request. No language certificate is required to apply: certificates can be submitted as additional qualifications.
Can I apply before completing my master's degree?
Yes, if you graduate by the date set in the call: for cycle XLII it was 31 October 2026. You are admitted with reservation and must obtain the degree before enrolling.
Do I need to contact a supervisor before applying?
No. Supervisors are appointed by the Faculty board after the first year. Our faculty's research interests can still help you shape a proposal that fits the programme.
How does the selection work?
The committee has 100 points: up to 45 for your university career (average grade, final grade and time to degree), up to 15 for other qualifications (study, research or work experience abroad, postgraduate qualifications, language certificates, publications) and up to 40 for the interview. Candidates with at least 30 points are invited to the interview, which assesses research aptitude and knowledge of the programme’s main fields, and discusses the research proposal. You pass with at least 60 points. For the reserved position, the CV is worth up to 40 points, reference letters up to 20 and the online interview up to 40. dal bando del XLII ciclo
Can I work during the PhD?
The PhD is a full-time commitment. Tutoring, supplementary teaching (up to 40 hours a year) and paid work need prior authorisation by the Faculty board, and the scholarship is not compatible with a personal income above its annual amount. See For PhD students.
I have a degree from abroad: what do I need?
To apply, certificates of your degrees with exams, grades and credits, translated into Italian or English. If you are admitted, to complete enrolment you also need the original degree certificate (or a certified copy) with an Italian translation and legalisation, and a Declaration of Value, a Diploma Supplement or a CIMEA statement of comparability.
I live outside Italy: do I have to come to Cagliari for the interview?
Interviews are normally held in person in Cagliari. If you cannot attend for justified reasons, the call allows the interview to be held by videoconference on Microsoft Teams, at the same date and time. Candidates for the reserved position are always interviewed online. dal bando del XLII ciclo
Where can I find help with housing and visas?
The University’s EURAXESS Service Centre (euraxess@unica.it) assists admitted international candidates with entry, visa and residence procedures: start them as soon as you are admitted. For student housing, see ERSU Cagliari, the regional agency for the right to university study.

8 April 2026
Awards

Fenicia Cossu wins a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Global Postdoctoral Fellowship

Fenicia Cossu, who earned her PhD in our programme (cycle XXXVI) and co-founded the University of Cagliari spin-off Next Generation Economics Insights (NGEi), has been awarded a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Global Postdoctoral Fellowship. Her project AUTON (Automation and Occupational Network) scored 98/100 and is funded for three years: two at Monash University in Melbourne, under the supervision of Prof. Michelle Rendall, and one back at the University of Cagliari with Prof. Alessio Moro.

AUTON studies how automation, robotics and artificial intelligence spread through the labour market along the links between occupations, changing jobs, wages and employment opportunities.

8 July 2024
Awards

ASSIOA award for the best PhD thesis to Matteo Opizzi

Matteo Opizzi (cycle XXXV) received the 2024 award for the best PhD thesis in business organisation from ASSIOA, the Italian association of scholars of business organisation. His thesis, Doctoral students in the entrepreneurial university: an untapped potential?, supervised by Prof. Michela Loi, shows how doctoral students can act as a bridge between universities and society.
